theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout: Both registries carry a participant-facing money statement in packetInstructions that no packet carried, and in both jurisdictions the statement answers the same question: whether money still owed on the case has to be cleared before the participant can file. It does not, in either state, and the record says so in each. vf53 measured zero hits for it across every guidance file and the delivered PDF text of both families. The harm is identical in shape too: a participant who owes money and is not told may wait, or not file at all, on a misunderstanding this repository already holds the answer to.
howTheRepairWasMade: Guidance only, in participant language, in the section of each guide that vf53 named. The registry entries are build directives addressed to the builder, not participant prose, so they were carried by substance rather than reproduced verbatim; printing a build directive into a participant guide is its own defect and the sibling il-seal-nonconv-set demonstrates it (see outOfScopeObservedNotActedOn). Because the identical Illinois directive sits on all three Illinois tracks, the Illinois sentence is rendered from ONE exported constant in scripts/lib/il-sealing-unpaid-financial-obligation.mjs and imported by all three builders, so the three families cannot drift apart and there is one place to change it. The two builders that read the registry (il-seal-2yr, il-seal-3yr) additionally call assertRegistryStillDirectsTheUnpaidFinancialObligationNote, which throws if the directive ever leaves the registry, so the build refuses rather than shipping a legal statement under an authority the record has dropped. il-seal-edu's builder does not read the registry and imports the constant alone.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.whatWasCarried: One paragraph, placed as the last paragraph of the guide's 'What it costs, and the waiver' section, which is the section vf53 named: '**Unpaid fines and fees do not delay sealing.** A sentence terminates notwithstanding any outstanding financial legal obligation; "terminate" at § 5.2(a)(1)(M) covers unsatisfactory as well as satisfactory termination. FEE_AND_WAIVER.whatWasCarried: One paragraph, placed as the last paragraph of the guide's 'What this costs' section, which is the section vf53 named: '**Unpaid court costs do not delay eligibility.** "Sentence" does not include payment of court costs, so unpaid court costs do not delay eligibility for this route. The committed Ohio legal review this packet is built from calls that a common and expensive misunderstanding, so this packet states it rather than leaving you to ask. FEE_AND_WAIVER.traceability: The directive is packetInstructions[1] of track oh_marijuana_expungement in data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json. Its provenance in data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/OH.memo.json is OH__LEGAL-REVIEW__STATEWIDE__ohio-record-clearing-legal-review__ASOF-2026-08-01__EN.md, heading HEADLINE FINDINGS 5. The 'payable at filing' clause is this track's own manualCompletionItems entry, whereInPacket 'Presented to the clerk at filing', and the indigency clause is rules.feeWaiver, 'Indigency excuses the fee under ORC 2953.321(G)'. The directive's own second sentence — that this is a common and expensive misunderstanding — is a build instruction, so it is rendered as attribution to the legal review rather than printed as participant prose.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.whatWasDeliberatelyNotSaid: The source sentence at HEADLINE FINDINGS 5 opens by defining final discharge as completion of the sentence, parole, fines and restitution, and the court-costs point qualifies that clock. That final-discharge half is NOT carried here, because § 2953.321 imposes no waiting period at all: this track's only waitingPeriods entry is 'none. The section imposes no waiting period; what it requires is that the disposition predate the effective date'. Describing a final-discharge clock in this guide would state a rule this route does not have. The court-costs point is carried; the clock it qualifies elsewhere is not imported into a route without one.

It therefore CANNOT see the defect vf53 found and cannot see the repair either. defectsObservedInTheVerifierItself: Exits 0 while printing FAIL. Confirmed on this run: a full-corpus pass printed 2 FAIL_MISSING_PREFILLS, 4 FAIL_ROUTE_SELECTION and 1 FAIL_MISSING_REQUIRED_FACTS and still exited 0. This is the defect the grant warned about and it reproduces exactly.

Those zeros are not measurements; on the same run the same nine counters printed UNMEASURED for il-seal-edu-set, so the tool is inconsistent about whether an unmeasured counter is 0 or UNMEASURED, and on this family it chose 0.

THIRD DEFECT, NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED AND FOUND HERE: it silently ignores a bare positional family argument. `node verify-packet-completeness.mjs il-seal-2yr-set` audits all 294 families and prints an identical whole-corpus report no matter which family is named, with no error and no warning. The filter is `--family <id>` (line 31, ARGS.indexOf('--family') + 1) and nothing validates leftover positionals. A lane that ran it the obvious way would read a 294-family corpus verdict and believe it had measured one family. Both forms were run here and both are reported above; the per-family verdicts come from the `--family` form.
Labels NOT_MEASURABLE_HERE with the word FAIL. 'this could not be measured' and 'this failed' are different claims and the row prefix conflates them.

whatThisLaneCouldNotRepair: oh_marijuana_expungement-set ships a SECOND builder-produced guidance file, tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/participant-instructions.md, which vf53 also searched and which still carries zero hits for the court-costs statement. It is written by trackInstructions() in the shared build host and it was confirmed to be live rather than stale: the rebuild rewrote it, byte-identically. It was left alone deliberately. By its own first line it is 'a statutory-content draft and review artifact', it has no 'What this costs' section, and it delegates the whole fee question in one line — 'Confirm the current filing fee and waiver practice. The frozen design records ...' — so it carries neither the $50/indigency statement that vf53 already scored PASS nor the new court-costs statement. Adding only the second would make it inconsistent in a new way rather than fixing it, and its content comes from a memoRequirements block that holds no court-costs field, so carrying the statement there would mean inventing a data field rather than rendering one. The honest position is that this family has two guidance surfaces and this repair reached one of them; whether the review artifact should carry participant money statements at all is a design question for the family's owner, not something this lane should settle by hand-editing generated output. companion/companion-guidance.md is silent for the same reason and was left for the same reason.
